chapter.title: Getting Started
chapter.para: This chapter installs the bridge, and runs the smallest programs in both directions: Rexx using .NET, and C# using Rexx.

section.title: Installing
section.para: You want to use .NET from your Rexx programs, without building anything.

How it works. You need ooRexx 5, 64-bit (rexx -v works in a terminal), and .NET 8 or later, 64-bit: the runtime is enough. On Windows, install the .NET Desktop Runtime, x64, which adds Windows Forms, from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download. The bridge comes from the project's releases page, https://github.com/JosepMariaBlasco/oorexxnet/releases.

On Windows, download oorexxnet-version-setup.exe and run it. It finds your ooRexx and .NET (and says where to get .NET if it is missing), installs the bridge into ooRexx, puts these books in ooRexx's doc folder and, with the samples, in ooRexx's Start menu folder, and can be uninstalled from Settings > Apps. It is not signed: Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" (More info, then Run anyway), as for ooRexx's own installer.
On any system, download the zip rexxnet-version.zip (Windows, Linux and macOS in one), unzip it, open a terminal in the folder rexxnet, and run its installer:

(As administrator on Windows, or with sudo on Linux and macOS, when ooRexx is in a system folder). It puts the bridge into the ooRexx that runs it, copies the samples into ooRexx's samples folder, under dotnet, checks it all, and ends with ooRexx/.NET: installed and OK. rexx oorexxnet-uninstall removes it.
For a .NET program that runs Rexx code, reference the NuGet package instead: dotnet add package Rexx.Net --prerelease. It needs an installed ooRexx.
See also Reference, Introduction, Windows, Linux and macOS.

section.title: Using .NET from Rexx
section.para: You want to call .NET from a Rexx program.

example.title: Using .NET from Rexx
example.programlisting:
say .net~System~Math~Sqrt(2) say .net~System~Environment~ProcessorCount > 0 sb = .net~System~Text~StringBuilder~new("Hello") sb~Append(", ")~Append("world")~Append("!") say sb~ToString "("sb~Length "characters)"
::requires "net.cls"

section.para: Run it as any Rexx program: rexx hello.rex.

How it works. ::requires "net.cls" loads the bridge, and defines &net;, the root of .NET's namespaces. Going down by name reaches a namespace (System), then a type (System.Math), whose messages are its static members: .net~System~Math~Sqrt(2) is C#'s Math.Sqrt(2). new makes an instance, whose messages are its members: a method call (sb~Append(", ")), or a property read (sb~Length). Names are caseless. Numbers come back as Rexx strings, and bools as .Boolean~true and .Boolean~false, which are 1 and 0 to Rexx: a .NET object is a Rexx object, and a .NET value a Rexx value.
See also Reference, Introduction, Names and Messages.

section.title: Running Rexx from C#
section.para: You want to run Rexx code from a C# program.

example.title: Running Rexx from C#

section.para: In a console project (dotnet new console) with the package (dotnet add package Rexx.Net --prerelease), run it with dotnet run.

How it works. RexxInterpreter.Create() creates an ooRexx interpreter instance, which using ends at the end. Run runs Rexx code as a routine: its arguments are USE ARG's, its RETURN is the result, converted by Run<int>. Compile keeps a routine to call many times. What the Rexx code says goes to the console, marked REXXout>, so that it stands out from the application's own output; takes it into the application instead.
See also Reference, .NET Using ooRexx: the Rexx.Net API.

section.title: Running the Samples
section.para: You want more programs to read and run.

How it works. The installer copies the project's samples into ooRexx's samples folder, under dotnet: rexx (every system: collections, files, regular expressions, JSON, events, tasks, the event thread), windows (Windows Forms, dialogs, the registry, the clipboard), office and libreoffice (each program written twice, with ooRexx's OLEObject and through the bridge), oorexx-ole (ooRexx's own OLE samples, through the bridge), oodialog-net (ooDialog's samples rewritten for Windows Forms, with a porting guide), and the C#, VB.NET and PowerShell programs that run Rexx. Each runs with rexx NAME.rex; most of them, given auto, run by themselves and close their windows. rexx check.rex checks the installation.
